guide:
Akari

Also called Light Up

Nikoli introduced Akari in 2001 under the Japanese name Bijutsukan, "art gallery", and outside Japan it goes by Akari, "light".

Place light bulbs so every white cell is lit and no bulb shines on another.

Rules

  1. A bulb lights its row and column, up to a black cell. Every white cell must be lit.

  2. No bulb may shine on another bulb.

  3. A number on a black cell says how many bulbs are right beside it (not diagonally).

  4. In a cipher, black cells show letters instead of numbers. Each letter stands for a number from 0 to 4: the same letter is always the same number, and different letters are different numbers. Work them out as you go.

Example: Lights On
